texts.facts: The Petitioner has filed this petition under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, seeking compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident dated 23.09.2022. 2. Due to accidental injuries he lost his income. The Turuvekere Police have registered a case against the driver of the offending vehicle in Cr.No.217/2022 P/U/Sec.279, 337, 304(A) of IPC. Therefore, the 1 st respondent being the RC Owner and the 2nd respondent being the Insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay Suresha vs Shekaraiah on 19 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/37445310/ 2 compensation to him. It has denied all the averments of the petition except admitting the issuance of the policy in favour of the Respondent No.1 in respect of the TATA ACE vehicle bearing KA-44-6841. The driver of the TATA Ace vehicle did not have valid and effective DL and also FC to ply the vehicle as on the date of accident. Further denied the nature of accident, involvement of the vehicle in the accident. There is non- compliance of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of the MV Act. Further, at the time of accident the petitioner was on a motorcycle without wearing safety headgear. It has also denied the age, occupation and the manner of accident. Therefore, prayed for dismissal of the petition against it.
texts.arguments: The counsel for the Respondent No.2 has relied upon the following decision: ILR 2010 KAR 2439 : Sri. Subhash Vs. The New India Assurance Co. Ltd., SCCH - 25 7 MVC No. 7019/2022 Suresha vs Shekaraiah on 19 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/37445310/ 3 9. iv) LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME:- The counsel for the Respondent No.2 relied on ILR 2010 KAR 2439 : Sri. Subhash Vs. The New India Assurance Co. Ltd., Wherein it is observed by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka that ' if the claimant has continued in service, then the question of awarding compensation towards loss of future income does not arise'. However in the case on hand, even if the petitioner has continued the Agricultural work it is clear from his evidence that the left hand has become useless and Agriculture requires lot of manual labor which can be done only if the both the hands and both the legs are normal. Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.4,11,060/- (Rs.15,500/- x 12 x 13 x 17%= Rs.4,11,060/-) under this head.

6. On the above rival contentions of the parties, this court has framed the following issues:-
1.

Whether the Petitioner proves that, the accident occurred on 23.09.2022 at 5.45pm due to rash and negligent driving of driver of TATA ACE Goods Vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-44-6841 and in the said accident petitioner sustained injuries?
Whether the Petitioner he is entitled for Compensation?

If so, to what extent and from whom?
3. What order or award?

On hearing both sides and perusal of the evidence on record this court answers the above issues as follows:-
 Issue No.1: In the Affirmative,

In order to prove that the accident occurred due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the TATA Ace Goods vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-44-6841, the petitioner has examined himself as PW.1 and got marked Exs.P.1 to P.5.
He has reiterated the contents of the petition in his affidavit filed in lieu of his chief examination.
During the cross examination of PW.1 nothing worthwhile is elicited to disprove that the accident caused due to the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.
On the other side, the respondents did not examine any witness nor produced documents to show there was negligence on the part of the petitioner.
11. As per FIR at Ex.P.1, it was registered on the next SCCH - 25 8 MVC No. 7019/2022 day of the accident on the complaint of one Nagesh - eye witness.

The IMV report at Ex.P.4 also shows that the TATA ACE Goods vehicle was damaged to its front left side bumper assembly, front left side headlight assembly and front left side body sheet assembly damaged.
The police have conducted investigation and filed the charge sheet as per Ex.P.5 against the driver of the TATA ACE Goods vehicle.
The petitioner has also examined MRO of Aadhichunchanagiri Hospital as PW.2 and got marked Exs.P.11 to 14, authorization letter, MLC Extract, police intimation and case sheet.
During his cross examination, nothing worthwhile is elicited.
The respondent No.2 has contended that the petitioner did not wear helmet as on the date of accident and there is sole negligence on the part of the petitioner himself.
Howevcer they have not led any evidence to prove the same.

Therefore, on the basis of all these documents the tribunal holds that there was negligence on the part of the driver of the TATA ACE Goods vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-44- SCCH - 25 9 MVC No. 7019/2022 6841.

In order to prove the injuries and disability suffered by the petitioner, the petitioner has produced the wound certificate at Ex.P.3.

Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for the above said amount under this head.

iii) LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID UP PERIOD:-
As mentioned above the petitioner has sustained grievous and simple injuries.
The petitioner has produced discharge summary at Ex.P.6 of Aadichunchanagiri Hospital to show the SCCH - 25 13 MVC No. 7019/2022 duration and treatment in the said hospital.
Therefore, considering the nature of injuries it can be said that the Petitioner may have required at least One month time for recovering from the injuries sustained by him.
Hence, he is entitled only for a sum of Rs.15,500/- under this head.
On perusal of Ex.P.7/Notarized copy of the petitioner, the petitioner's birth year is mentioned as 1973 and the accident SCCH - 25 14 MVC No. 7019/2022 occurred on 23.09.2022.
As such, petitioner's age is considered as 49 years.
Therefore, as on the date of the accident the Petitioner's age is 49 years.
As per the dictum laid down in Sarala Verma's case the appropriate multiplier applicable to his age is 13.

(v) LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND  HAPPINESS:-
The Petitioner was aged about 49 years at the time of accident.
He has sustained grievous and simple injuries and as per consideration of this Tribunal, he is suffering from 17% functional disability.
The Petitioner has to suffer this disability throughout his life.
Because of this he will have to lose some of the amenities and comforts.

Therefore, considering the age and nature of injuries that the Petitioner has suffered,

If it is rounded off it comes to Rs.5,90,100/- and same is awarded under to the Petitioner.
The Respondents did not prove their defence as discussed above.
Therefore, the Respondents being the owner and the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.
However, as the policy existed as on the date of accident, the respondent No.2/insurer has to indemnify the respondent No.1/insured and has to pay compensation awarded to the petitioner.

The Petitioner has claimed for a sum of Rs.20,00,000/-

Accordingly, Issue No.2 is held in the affirmative.
19. Issue No.3:-

For the reasons and discussions made above and finding to the above issues, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following:-
ORDER
The petition is allowed in part with cost.

The Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.5,90,100/- (Rupees Five Lakhs Ninety Thousand and One Hundred only) along with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of depositing the amount.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the said compensation to the petitioner.
